`make test-test_perf_buffer` ends with `#296 perf_buffer:OK` — `Summary: 1/0 PASSED, 0 SKIPPED, 0 FAILED`. (The SKIP-TEST / skel.h errors above it are pre-existing harness noise from unrelated tests, not from this object.)

The translation in `progs/test_perf_buffer.rs`:
- **`my_pid_map`** — `ARRAY`, `key`/`value` `int`, `max_entries` 1; **`perf_buf_map`** — `PERF_EVENT_ARRAY` with no `max_entries` member, so libbpf sizes it to the possible-CPU count that `perf_buffer__new()` depends on.
- **`handle_sys_enter`** in `tp/raw_syscalls/sys_enter` — grabs the CPU id, looks up `my_pid_map[0]`, bails with `1` on null or pid mismatch, otherwise emits the `int` cpu via `bpf_perf_event_output(ctx, &perf_buf_map, BPF_F_CURRENT_CPU, ...)`. Returns `1` on every path, matching C.
- Helpers are the fn-pointer-transmute idiom (`get_smp_processor_id`=8, `get_current_pid_tgid`=14, `map_lookup_elem`=1, `perf_event_output`=25); the pid comparison is done as `i32` to match C's implicit truncation of the `>> 32` result.
